title: Quantile-based SLI pipeline and multi-region failover decisioning
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We need an observability and decisioning pipeline that supports quantile-based SLIs for token-level latency and drives automated multi-region failover and circuit-breaker actions. Current metrics are count/avg-focused and miss tail behavior across shards and regions; this impairs our ability to trigger graceful degradation before customer-visible outages.

Goal: Build an end-to-end pipeline that collects compact quantile sketches at the edge, aggregates them across shards/regions/models, exposes p50/p95/p99 and continuous quantile heatmaps in Grafana, and feeds a decision engine that can trigger region failover, model fallback, or progressive load-shedding. Provide a set of dashboards, alert rules, and a runbook for on-call.

Non-goals: Full per-request token trace across every request (we will sample); architecting transport-level routing (handled by smart-routing workstream).

Success criteria: 1) Accurate cross-region p95/p99 per-model and per-route within 5% of full histogram when compared in a controlled sample; 2) Dashboards and heatmaps visible in Console with drill-down by region/shard/model within 30s of ingestion; 3) Automated decisioning triggers defined and validated in canary; 4) On-call runbook validated via game day with one simulated failover and one load-shed scenario.
tasks: Instrument edge proxies to emit per-request token latency sketches (t-digest or HDR) with route/model tags
Implement sample-reservoir + deterministic sampling key (customer_id) to bound cardinality
Ingest sketches into metrics pipeline and compute p50/p95/p99 + continuous quantile rollups per region/shard/model
Expose Grafana panels: quantile heatmap, shard-level histograms, regional comparison, rolling SLO gauge
Build decision engine that consumes aggregated quantiles and error-rate signals and emits failure actions (failover, model-fallback, shed) via feature-flagged endpoint
Create alerting and autoscaling hooks for canary and production
Author runbook and conduct game-day test
acceptance_criteria: Prometheus/Grafana panels render quantile heatmap with <=30s ingestion latency
Decision engine triggers a simulated region failover in canary under synthetic load and falls back according to policy
Measured end-to-end quantile error vs full-sample baseline < 5% for p95/p99 in validation test
Runbook contains clear steps for surge, failover, and rollback and is linked from Console
decisions: Use t-digest sketches at the edge for quantile aggregation to minimize payload size and preserve tail fidelity
Sample deterministically by customer_id with a default 2% reservoir to control cardinality; sample rate to be feature-flag adjustable per route
Separate SLI buckets for 'initial token' latency and 'continuation token' latency because distribution differs significantly
Aggregate sketches at shard-level then region-level; compute cross-region rollups using mergeable sketches
Decision thresholds: candidate SLOs p95 < 120ms, p99 < 350ms per token for hosted API; circuit opens when p99 > 2x SLO for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows AND error rate > 0.5%
When circuit opens, policy order: 1) fallback to compatible model quantized variant, 2) route eligible requests to dedicated queued path, 3) shed best-effort (non-critical) traffic by customer tier
tradeoffs: Sketching reduces cardinality and bandwidth but may slightly bias extreme tail estimates compared to full traces
Deterministic sampling prevents customer-level starvation but requires per-customer keying and coordination at proxies
Aggressive automated failover reduces customer impact for most users but may cause flapping if thresholds are too tight — mitigated with conservative hysteresis and cooldown windows

notes: Incident learnings: during 2025-11 outage we saw high tail on continuation tokens due to KV cache thrash; decoupling initial/continuation SLIs will help target mitigations
PR feedback: unit tests must include merge correctness for sketches and a deterministic seed for sampling tests
